summary: The Central Government will set up a special group called the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal through an official notice. This body will have a chairperson and several judicial and technical members chosen by the government. Its main job is to listen to appeals against certain orders and decisions made by the Tribunal, the National Financial Reporting Authority, and under the Competition Act, 2002.
points: The Central Government must create an Appellate Tribunal by official notification.
The body will be called the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal.
It will consist of a chairperson and a number of judicial and technical members chosen by the Central Government.
The tribunal hears appeals against orders of the Tribunal or the National Financial Reporting Authority under this Act.
The tribunal also hears appeals against directions, decisions, or orders under section 53A of the Competition Act, 2002.
example: A company called Meera Textiles Private Limited received an unfavourable order from the National Financial Reporting Authority under the Companies Act, 2013. Unhappy with this decision, the directors decided to challenge the outcome. According to the law, they can file an appeal against this order. This appeal will be heard by the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, which is the special body set up by the Central Government consisting of a chairperson and judicial and technical members.

terms.meaning: A higher official body that has the power to review and hear challenges against decisions made by a lower authority.
An official public announcement or formal notice issued by the government.
Qualified individuals appointed to the tribunal who have legal or specialized technical expertise.

watch: People often confuse the Appellate Tribunal with the original Tribunal, but the Appellate Tribunal is specifically meant for hearing challenges against earlier orders.
